slides.title: Network Architectures
content: Network architecture defines how devices communicate, share resources, and perform tasks within a network
Client-server architecture uses a centralized server to provide resources and services to multiple clients with better control and security
Peer-to-peer architecture is decentralized where each device acts as both client and server, enabling direct resource sharing
Hybrid architecture combines centralized control and decentralized sharing for better scalability and reliability

slides.title: Network Design Principles
content: Network design is the process of planning a network to ensure scalability, reliability, performance, and security
Scalability allows networks to grow by adding devices, subnets, and services without major redesign
Reliability ensures continuous operation using redundancy and failover mechanisms
Security protects networks using firewalls, encryption, and access control while manageability simplifies monitoring and maintenance

slides.title: Load Balancing & CDN
content: Load balancing distributes incoming traffic across multiple servers to prevent overload and improve performance
Techniques include round robin, least connections, IP hashing, and dynamic load balancing based on server conditions
Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) use geographically distributed servers to deliver content faster by reducing latency
CDNs cache content on edge servers and improve scalability, reliability, and user experience

slides.title: Network Virtualization
content: Network virtualization abstracts physical network resources into virtual networks for better flexibility and efficiency
It enables multiple virtual networks to run on the same physical infrastructure using VLANs, VPNs, and overlay networks
It improves resource utilization, scalability, and security through logical segmentation
It is widely used in cloud computing, data centers, and multi-tenant environments

slides.title: Software Defined Networking (SDN)
content: SDN is a networking approach that separates the control plane from the data plane for centralized and programmable management
The SDN controller acts as the brain of the network, managing traffic flow and policies dynamically
It enables automation, flexibility, and efficient resource allocation using software-based configuration
It is used in data centers, cloud environments, and large-scale enterprise networks

slides.title: Network Reliability & Fault Tolerance
content: Network reliability ensures consistent network operation with minimal downtime and high availability
Fault tolerance allows networks to continue functioning even when components fail using redundancy and failover
Techniques include backup devices, multiple paths, load balancing, clustering, and error detection mechanisms
Metrics like availability, MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures), and MTTR (Mean Time to Repair) measure reliability
